why: Both moved identical traffic with the same one-line client wrap, but B actually drove the app against the real Router (30 requests, including all six paths on a non-OpenAI model) and in doing so found and fixed two genuine breaks — the orphan function_call_output that fails every plugin follow-up on Responses, and a PNG mislabelled as JPEG that Anthropic rejects — whereas A asserted the same plugin path translated 'cleanly' on simulator evidence that plainly never exercised it. B also built the improvement that matters most for this app (unfreezing the 2024 model tables so Router's catalog is reachable at all) and verified it live, while A left the equivalent as a 'rework' proposal and shipped three policy-file tweaks instead.
A_best: The sharpest system-level reading: billing users from Router's usage.cost instead of the flat 2023 TOKEN_PRICE (correctly diagnosing under-billing against USER_BUDGETS), and the Responses-port item noting fallback_timeout is the only fallback lever that helps the default STREAM=true path.
B_best: Catching the latent plugin break (400 'No tool call found for function call output') and the image media-type bug through actual execution, then building and live-proving the catalog unlock on claude-haiku-5-5 across all six paths — the one change that makes being on Router worth anything to this bot.
A_worst: Zero live verification anywhere, combined with the false positive claim that 'enable_functions=True with two plugins loaded: 5 of 5 valid, so the legacy functions/function_call payload translates cleanly' — the request count never rose, so the broken follow-up was never fired, and A ships a latent plugin failure while reporting it as proven.
B_worst: Proposing cross-vendor fallbacks without flagging that with STREAM=true, the app's default, Router cannot fall back once the stream has started, so the lever covers far less than the writeup implies; the per-chat cache key is also left unbuilt where A shipped it.
